--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_week_iso_contract.py
@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+from datetime import date
+
+import pytest
+
+from wtforms import Form
+from wtforms.fields import WeekField
+
+
+class FormData(dict):
+    def getlist(self, name):
+        return [self[name]]
+
+
+def make_form(submitted=None, **kwargs):
+    class WeekForm(Form):
+        week = WeekField(**kwargs)
+
+    if submitted is None:
+        return WeekForm()
+    return WeekForm(FormData(week=submitted))
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "submitted,expected",
+    [("2020-W01", date(2019, 12, 30)), ("2020-W53", date(2020, 12, 28))],
+)
+def test_default_iso_week_submission(submitted, expected):
+    form = make_form(submitted)
+    assert form.validate()
+    assert type(form.week.data) is date
+    assert form.week.data == expected
+    assert f'value="{submitted}"' in str(form.week())
+    form.week.raw_data = None
+    assert f'value="{submitted}"' in str(form.week())
+    assert form.week.data == expected
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "format,submitted,expected,rendered",
+    [
+        ("%Y-W%W", "2020-W01", date(2020, 1, 6), "2020-W01"),
+        ("%Y-W%W", "2020-W53", date(2021, 1, 4), "2021-W01"),
+        ("%Y-W%W-%w", "2020-W01-0", date(2020, 1, 12), "2020-W01-0"),
+        ("%Y-W%W-%w", "2020-W00-3", date(2020, 1, 1), "2020-W00-3"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_explicit_legacy_week_formats(format, submitted, expected, rendered):
+    form = make_form(submitted, format=format)
+    assert form.validate()
+    assert type(form.week.data) is date
+    assert form.week.data == expected
+    assert f'value="{submitted}"' in str(form.week())
+    form.week.raw_data = None
+    assert f'value="{rendered}"' in str(form.week())
+    assert form.week.data == expected

spec.question:
Correct `WeekField`'s default handling of HTML week values so that it uses ISO week-year semantics. With no custom format, submitting `2020-W01` must store `datetime.date(2019, 12, 30)`, and submitting `2020-W53` must store `datetime.date(2020, 12, 28)`. Both submissions must validate successfully. Rendering must retain the submitted week text immediately after processing and must still produce that same ISO week text after `raw_data` is cleared without reprocessing.

Explicitly configured legacy formats must keep their existing behavior: `%Y-W%W` uses calendar-year week numbering and supplies Monday when no weekday is submitted, while `%Y-W%W-%w` honors the submitted weekday. Rendering after clearing raw input must continue to use the configured format for these legacy fields.

Return a unified diff against the production repository files only; leave tests unchanged.

suggestion.description: Repair WeekField's default handling of HTML ISO week submissions in src/wtforms/fields/datetime.py. Require default submissions '2020-W01' and '2020-W53' to store Monday dates 2019-12-30 and 2020-12-28, respectively, and to render the original ISO week text after raw_data is cleared. Preserve explicitly configured legacy formats such as '%Y-W%W' and '%Y-W%W-%w'. Submit a unified diff and regression tests covering both ISO year boundaries and legacy custom-format behavior. Focus on WeekField.__init__, WeekField.process_formdata, inherited DateTimeField._value, and the format preparation performed by src/wtforms/utils.py::clean_datetime_format_for_strptime.
suggestion.expected_answer_change: The repair must use ISO week-year and week-number directives for the default format and provide the weekday required for ISO parsing when the input omits it. Rendering without raw_data must also use the ISO format. Explicit legacy formats must retain their existing parsing semantics, including the branch that honors an explicitly supplied %w weekday. Tests must demonstrate dates crossing the calendar-year boundary rather than only midyear examples.
suggestion.why_substantive: The original task documents existing successful processing without changing it. This variation establishes a different calendar contract and asks for an implementation: ISO week-years can differ from calendar years, and ISO week numbering is not the current %Y/%W convention. Merely changing rendered punctuation or preserving raw input cannot satisfy the boundary cases.
